failure_summary.description: Stray `]` at the end of the last object (`...}]]}]`) made the whole answer unparseable (score 0) in two trajectories. A third emitted a duplicate `"optional parameters"` key that wiped out the earlier list. Several objects also omitted the `optional parameters` key.
Used `Provider — endpoint` (em dash) names such as `Lost Ark — get classes`, even though the query quoted the exact `Provider: Endpoint` form. All five tool names scored zero.

Collapsed 'auto-complete on both Asos and Wayfair' into one Wayfair call. Fanned two unnamed-store searches out across Asos, Shopee and Lazada instead of one fitting marketplace each. Used Numbers Translator instead of Numbers math/trivia fact tools.
Emitted tool names the query mentioned (GetFutureEvents, GetFAQsByTopic) that are not in the tool list.
Missed page 1/page 2 for the repeated reviews call. Used `UK` instead of `uk`. Omitted stated qualifiers such as the Card Draw and GamerPower optionals.

patch.reasoning: Parse failures and duplicate keys cost the most (full-task zero or lost params) and recur despite the existing rules, so I add a literal BAD/GOOD end-of-answer self-check at the very end, where it is less likely to be skipped. The em-dash tool-name failure zeroed every tool even when the query quoted the right name, so I tighten the first Output-format bullet with a verbatim-copy rule. Two missing/extra-call patterns (named multiple providers, unnamed store searches, hallucinated endpoints) go into 'Which calls to make'. Numbers fact tools and repeat-call paging go into 'Tool selection'. Everything is short and generalizable, and none of it duplicates the protected section.

edits.target: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely.
edits.content: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely. The separator is a colon plus space (`: `), never an em dash. BAD `Lost Ark — get classes`; GOOD `Lost Ark: get classes`. If the query already quotes `'Provider: Endpoint'`, copy it verbatim. Only emit names that exist as `### ` headings in the tool list; never invent an endpoint the list lacks.

- Number facts: 'mathematical properties/facts about N' -> `Numbers: Get math fact`; 'trivia about N' -> `Numbers: Get trivia fact` (one call per number). `Numbers Translator` only spells digits as words; never use it for facts.
- The same endpoint requested twice with different settings (e.g. reviews 'sorted by most helpful', later 'more reviews sorted by most recent') means two calls: page `1` then page `2`, each with its own sort_order.

edits.target: - Do not add 'helper', 'random', 'new releases' or 'list' calls that no clause names.
edits.content:
- A clause naming several providers ('auto-complete on both Asos and Wayfair') means one call per named provider, each to that provider's own endpoint (`Asos: v2/auto-complete` AND `Wayfair: auto-complete`). Never collapse them into one.
- When the query says 'search for X and Y' without naming a store, give each item ONE call to the single marketplace whose catalog fits it (clothing -> Asos; furniture, lamps, home -> Wayfair search). Do not fan each item out across Shopee, Lazada, AliExpress and others.
- If the query quotes an endpoint name that is not a heading in the list (e.g. GetFutureEvents), do not invent it. Use a listed sibling only when its description matches the clause, otherwise make no call for it.

## Final self-check (run on the finished answer, character by character)
1. BAD: `{"name": "kun", "value": "oya"}]]}]`. A stray `]` makes the whole answer unparseable and scores 0. GOOD: `{"name": "kun", "value": "oya"}], "optional parameters": []}]`.
2. BAD: `"optional parameters": [{"name": "page", "value": "1"}], "optional parameters": []}`. The second key erases the first list. GOOD: `"optional parameters": [{"name": "page", "value": "1"}]}`.
3. BAD: an object with `"required parameters": [...]` and no `"optional parameters"` key. Every object ends `"optional parameters": [...]}`, using `[]` when empty. A call with no params at all is `{"tool name": "X: Y", "required parameters": [], "optional parameters": []}`.
4. Each list closes with exactly one `]`, each object with exactly one `}`, and the whole answer is `[{...}, {...}]`.
5. Every tool name has `: ` and no ` — `. The object count equals the number of request clauses, including the last sentence.
